response:
Carbon taxes and cap-and-trade schemes are two primary market-based instruments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. 

A carbon tax imposes a fee on fossil fuel emissions, typically per ton of CO2. Companies pay the tax, which increases their costs and incentivizes emissions reduction. Revenue can be used to fund clean energy projects or compensate low-income households.

A cap-and-trade scheme sets an overall emissions cap, allocating permits to companies. Companies can buy or sell permits, creating a market. If a company exceeds its cap, it must purchase additional permits, while those under their cap can sell excess permits, encouraging emissions reduction.
